newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold volume jumps, prices mixed.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold volume jumps, prices mixed.

text.p: Traded volume on the Istanbul gold exchange more than doubled to 1,825 kg on Tuesday from Monday's 830 kg on continuing physical demand from the free market and banks' arbitrage deals, dealers said.
Gold closed at $355.00 an ounce, down sharply from $358.00 on Monday, but rose in lira terms to 1,400,600 lira per gram versus 1,397,500, helped by the lira weakening against the dollar.

"There was continuing demand from the free market and volume increased greatly as seller banks brought gold onto the market, easing the shortage that had been in the market for the last week," one dealer said.
Dealers said banks also arbitraged as gold fell in dollar terms and rose in lira.
The Turkish lira closed little changed at 121,200 to the dollar, compared to 121,180 on Monday.
Of the day's trade, 770 kg were traded in the morning session and 1,055 in the afternoon. 75.6 percent of trade was conducted in dollar terms.
